title: Machine configuration edges
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a finite Boolean string, and let $s,u,v$ be natural numbers. Declare $(u,v)$ to be an edge at input $x$ and parameter $s$ if at least one of the following holds: $u=0$, $v\ge2$, and the encoding of $x$ together with the encoding of the binary representations of $v-2$ and $s$ belongs to the initial language of $N$; or $u\ge2$, $v=1$, and the corresponding encoding using $u-2$ belongs to its accepting language; or $u,v\ge2$ and $N$ makes a step from configuration $u-2$ to configuration $v-2$ on input $x$ with parameter $s$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet
caveat: The snippet does not define the encoding, initial and accepting languages, or step relation.
